decision_summary.text: Whether to accept a small public exhibition while the siblings' selection authority, consent boundaries, and public framing remain unsettled.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The exhibition might be designed around a limited period or theme where the evidence and permissions are stronger, leaving contested material in the archive for later work.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I am leaning toward accepting the slot, choosing a narrow theme about the family's first ten years in the neighborhood, and limiting the exhibition to material that Tomas and I both support displaying.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant

threads.text: Whether Mara's father's letter can be displayed against her specific objection.

introduced.speaker: user
introduced.quote: Our cousin Mara does not want a letter from her father displayed, even though Tomas says it explains why that branch of the family left.

responses.speaker: assistant
responses.quote: Mara's objection is specific and should be treated as real, while the broader question of who can speak for shared material remains unresolved.

responses.speaker: user
responses.quote: We would invite relatives to comment on draft captions and preserve disagreements where they matter, but not give everyone veto over the whole exhibition.

constraints.text: Captions are incomplete and some family stories conflict.

source_evidence.speaker: user

constraints.text: The center accepts a twenty-item exhibition with provisional captions or conflicting versions.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: The cultural center says the exhibition can be small—perhaps twenty items—and they are comfortable showing captions as provisional or including two versions of a story.

constraints.text: The center needs a commitment within one month to reserve the spring slot.

source_evidence.speaker: user

constraints.text: The user's mother would like to participate actively in something public; no health condition is stated.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I also learned that our mother would like to see something public while she can still participate actively.

constraints.text: The mother tends to smooth conflict and may favor captions other relatives dispute.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: At the same time, she tends to smooth conflict and may support captions that other relatives dispute.

constraints.text: The user worries that a small selection will still become the family's public identity to strangers.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: The cultural center says the exhibition can be small—perhaps twenty items—and they are comfortable showing captions as provisional or including two versions of a story. They need a commitment in a month to reserve the spring slot. Tomas sees that flexibility as answering my concern. I feel relieved and also suspicious of my relief, because twenty items still create a frame. Whatever we choose becomes “our family” to strangers who will not see the rest.

constraints.text: The meaning of mutual support remains unresolved when one sibling calls an object essential and the other calls it unsuitable.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I have not decided what “both support” means if Tomas thinks a disputed object is essential and I think the dispute itself makes it unsuitable.
